content.content: 7:Our framework assumes non-differential misclassification: $P(A^*|A, Y, \mathbf{Z}) = P(A^*|A)$. This holds when the LLM annotator has no access to the outcome $Y$, but may be violated when few-shot examples are selected conditional on $Y$ or when annotation difficulty varies with the outcome. A stress test on the exposure topology (Appendix~\ref{sec:nondiff_stress}) shows moderate robustness: at $\varepsilon{=}0.05$ differential perturbation, violation rates increase by fewer than 3 percentage points. Under larger departures, the bias expressions provide an upper bound rather than an exact characterization. Closed-form bias expressions are derived for $K{=}3$ and verified numerically at $K{=}5,7$; expressions for arbitrary $K$ remain open. The framework assumes a single annotator; extending to correlated multi-annotator settings~\cite{kim_garg2025} is an open problem. The empirical validation spans $K{=}2,3,10$ with four LLMs, confirming the theoretical bias ranking, sign-flip guarantees, and $F_1$ disconnect across all $K$; however, VAST and CivilComments use a 7B model rather than frontier models, limiting direct cross-tier comparisons.
